- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1-2 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x prior peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast shows sharp upward trend after 3+ consecutive days of rising prices, reduce slope; if falling, avoid premature bottoming.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movement; increase forecast tail end by 0.5–1.0% per day if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.27” values, model tends to ignore sentiment; force a small upward bias (0.3–0.7) if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is clearly bearish (≥3 consecutive 0.00 or 0.27) and price has recently broken below 65.00.
